as_read: Null for cardiovascular outcomes: the trial record and two meta-analyses find no cardiovascular benefit, with cholesterol lowering and one myocardial infarction signal, and the only exposures are oils or food replacing saturated fat.

quote.text: An updated meta-analysis of linoleic acid intervention trials showed no evidence of cardiovascular benefit.

proposed_decision_text: All six labels print linoleic acid as a fatty acid row inside an oil or omega blend, not as an added active: EfaGold hemp oil 8 g, MEGA 3/6/9 oil blend 540 mg on three labels, Arctic Repair lingonberry seed oil 500 mg, and Multi-Oil 217 mg. In the Sydney Diet Heart recovered data (23386268), replacing saturated fat with safflower oil linoleic acid in 458 men after a coronary event gave higher all-cause mortality on the primary outcome, and its updated meta-analysis showed no cardiovascular benefit. The Minnesota Coronary Experiment recovery (27071971) lowered serum cholesterol but its meta-analysis of five trials showed no benefit on coronary or all-cause death. The Cochrane review (30488422) found increased omega-6 fats may make little or no difference to all-cause mortality or cardiovascular events, and reports two conflicting signals: a possible reduction in myocardial infarction (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.02, low quality) and lower total cholesterol. These are conflicting surrogate and subgroup signals with no clear clinical benefit. The trials gave linoleic acid as dietary oils or margarine replacing other fats, and 23386268 and 27071971 did not test a supplement at the labels' amounts, so this is the best available evidence rather than a test of these exact products.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: All-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality and cardiovascular events
studies_to_add.quote: We found no evidence that increasing omega-6 fats reduces cardiovascular outcomes other than MI, where 53 people may need to increase omega-6 fat intake to prevent 1 person from experiencing MI.

stop_list: Fields can't say the row is a fraction of an oil, so the fatty acid can't be separated from its carrier.

Labels also carry joint, skin and metabolic purposes (MEGA 3/6/9, Arctic Repair, Multi-Oil). The search returned no on-target oral linoleic acid trial for joint or skin in what I read, and this null covers cardiovascular outcomes only.
clinician_items: 23386268: replacing saturated fat with linoleic acid raised all-cause (HR 1.62), cardiovascular and coronary mortality in 458 men after a coronary event.
27071971: 22% higher risk of death for each 30 mg/dL cholesterol reduction in covariate adjusted Cox regression models.
21118617: n-6 specific diets, RR 1.13 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.53) for non-fatal MI plus CHD death; authors say advice to raise n-6 may increase risk of CHD and death.

33933722 and 40058591 used 15 to 20 g/d linoleic acid from safflower oil; 40058591 reports a relative systolic pressure difference favouring n-3 over n-6 (-1.81% vs 2.61%, P = 0.003). Read to the cut only.
stored_rating_note: Stored mixed is defensible only through surrogates. The stored rows are one negative and one null trial record, and the applicability text calls the trials 'supplemental', while both replaced dietary saturated fat with oils or margarine.
unread_notes: Abstracts only. 33933722, 40058591 and 35791734 cut at 1700 characters; 35791734 is evening primrose oil, not used. Searches returned 127 (25 listed) and 15.
